keyAndScale.modalCharacter: E Mixolydian with I - ♭VII - IV pub rock drive, shifting to the relative minor C#m for melodic pre-chorus emotion

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D
scalesUsed.application: Drives the main signature riff and driving verse rhythm, utilizing the natural flat-7th (D) for classic Australian rock drive
Shapes the triumphant, singing opening twin-guitar melody that introduces the track
Adds gritty blues bite and vocal responsive fills during the screaming high-energy guitar solo

mainProgression.description: The quintessential Australian anthem progression combining open string bass drones with bright ringing triads

sectionProgressions.description: Soaring twin-guitar harmonized melody soaring above a chugging E5 power chord rhythm foundation
Steady 8th-note driving groove supporting the storytelling narrative of life on the touring road
Melodic minor climb that builds longing emotional tension before bursting into the celebratory chorus
Full-throttle stadium pub rock chorus with soaring three-part vocal harmonies and roaring open chords

harmonicFunction: E (Tonic I): Welcoming home key established with warm low E open string authority and ringing sustain
D (Subtonic ♭VII): Injects the signature Mixolydian rock flavor, bypassing classical leading-tone stiffness
A (Subdominant IV): Uplifting release that resolves smoothly back down to the tonic E
C#m (Relative Minor vi): Introduces emotional weight and melodic pathos during the pre-chorus transition
B (Dominant V): Creates the essential tension and suspense that propels the arrangement back into E

techniques.name: Twin-Guitar Melodic Voicing
techniques.description: Harmonizing lyrical major pentatonic lead lines in diatonic thirds and sixths over a steady power-chord rhythm

notes: Lock into the 136 BPM tempo with precise alternate picking
Let each melodic note ring cleanly without colliding into neighboring strings
Apply expressive finger vibrato to all sustained whole notes

techniques.name: Dynamic Sectional Transitioning
techniques.description: Managing the shift between palm-muted verse chugging, tight pre-chorus barre chords, and wide-open chorus strumming

notes: Keep the right hand anchored lightly for the verse palm muting
Barre the 4th fret cleanly for the C#m pre-chorus chord
Open up the picking sweep completely when hitting the chorus

sections.name: Melodic Twin-Guitar Intro Hook
sections.description: One of the most recognizable guitar hooks in Australian rock, pairing a singing E major pentatonic melody with driving rhythm chords
notes: Anchor the open low E string as a continuous rhythmic driver
Play the melodic lead on the G and B strings at the 9th and 7th frets
Let the final E power chord ring with warm tube saturation

sections.name: Driving 8th-Note Verse
sections.description: A punchy, unyielding pub rock groove moving steadily through E, D, and A with crisp right-hand muting
notes: Rest the edge of your palm across the low E and A strings for controlled muting
Accentuate beats 2 and 4 to lock in with the snare drum backbeat
Release the mute cleanly on the chord change transitions

sections.name: Minor-Key Pre-Chorus Lift
sections.description: The emotional turning point of the song, stepping through C#m, B, and A to generate dramatic anticipation for the chorus
notes: Form a clean 4th-fret barre chord for the C#m chord shape
Step down smoothly to the B major barre chord at the 2nd fret
Crescendo through the final B chord to launch the chorus with explosive impact

sections.name: Anthemic Singalong Chorus
sections.description: The celebratory peak of the track, roaring with full-spectrum open guitar chords and huge crowd-chant energy
notes: Strike the open E chord with full downward pick sweeps across all six strings
Transition cleanly to open D and open A major voicings
Let the ringing open high E and B strings shimmer over the chord changes

sections.name: Stephen 'Fess' Parker's Blazing Pentatonic Solo
sections.description: Stephen 'Fess' Parker unleashes an energetic Aussie pub rock guitar solo, packed with blistering E minor pentatonic blues curls, high whole-step bends at the 15th and 17th frets, and crying vibrato.
notes: Start on the high E string at fret 12 and bend fret 15 of the B string with wide vibrato
Rip through the 12th-fret E minor pentatonic box with fast alternate picking
Climb into the upper register at frets 17 and 19 for the soaring solo climax
Resolve cleanly onto the open E power chord as the final chorus erupts

sections.name: Outro Jam & Guitar Heroics
sections.technique: Cranked Power Chords & High Pentatonic Fills
sections.description: The Radiators ride out on an exhilarating high-octane pub rock groove, with Fess Parker weaving searing lead fills around Brian Nichol's crowd chant.
sections.progression: E - D - A - E (repeating to end)
notes: Maintain maximum downstroke drive through the repeating E - D - A cadence
Toss in 15th-to-12th fret blues licks between the vocal calls
Hit the final sustained E major power chord with roaring Marshall tube saturation

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster or Gibson Les Paul Standard
guitar.pickup: Bridge pickup for crunchy driving rhythm; middle/neck pickup for warm intro lead chime

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50W Master Volume into 4x12 cabinet with Celestion G12M Greenbacks
alternatives: Fender Twin Reverb with overdrive pedal

effects.distortion: Organic valve overdrive boosted with an MXR Micro Amp or Ibanez Tube Screamer
effects.reverb: Subtle studio spring reverb for depth and spatial spread
effects.other: Analog bucket-brigade chorus pedal engaged subtly during the melodic intro hook

beginner.title: Open Chords & Main Progression
steps: Learn the open E, D, and A major chord shapes
Practice smooth 4-beat changes between E, D, and A at 100 BPM
Strum in steady eighth notes with consistent volume

intermediate.title: Barre Chords & Song Dynamics
steps: Master the C#m and B barre chords in the pre-chorus
Execute the dynamic transition from palm-muted verse to wide-open chorus
Perform the full rhythm track at the original 136 BPM tempo

advanced.title: Melodic Intro & Lead Fills
steps: Learn the opening melodic hook in E Major Pentatonic at the 9th fret
Incorporate the vocal responsive fills during the verse transitions
Perform both rhythm and lead parts seamlessly with authentic pub swagger

commonMistakes: Letting the D and A chords bleed into each other during the fast verse changes
Stumbling on the transition into the 4th-fret C#m barre chord in the pre-chorus
Rushing the tempo during the open chord chorus strums
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Open chord transition warm-up (E - D - A)
10 mins: Pre-chorus barre chord shifting drill (C#m - B - A) with a metronome at 110 BPM
10 mins: Melodic intro lead hook precision practice at the 9th fret
5 mins: Full song playthrough locking into the 136 BPM groove
focusAreas: Crisp muting between verse chord stabs
Clean finger placement on the C#m barre chord to avoid muted high strings
Singing vibrato on the sustained intro melody notes
metronomeWork: Start at 105 BPM to ensure clean barre chord execution in the pre-chorus
Gradually increase tempo to 120 and 130 BPM
Lock into 136 BPM focusing on relaxed right-hand strumming mechanics
